title.en: The Annals Hide in the Mountains

summaryEn: After a king died, officials turned the historians' notes into the Annals and guarded the books in archives far away in the mountains. Hoya follows the Annals from draft to mountain archive.
learningGoalsEn: Understand that each king's Annals were compiled after his death by a temporary office, the 실록청 (Sillokcheong).
Know that used drafts were destroyed (in early Joseon, washed in a stream: 세초) to keep secrets and reuse paper.
Know that copies were kept in several archives (사고), many deep in the mountains, and that two scholars saved the Jeonju copy during a war.
Know that historians aired the books in the sun every few years (포쇄) and packed them with herbs.
Learn the words 사고, 산, 책, 햇볕 and 약초.

origin.noteEn: Heritage history, researched from the sources listed on the Sources screen.

review.advisoryNoteEn: Mentions a king's death and a war in which some books were lost, told briefly and with no violent detail.

keywords.en: We dry the books in the sunshine.

scenes.narrationEn: When a king died, the next king's court set up a temporary office called the {kw:sillokcheong}. Its officials collected the historians' {kw:sacho} and other court records to write the late king's Annals.
scenes.captionEn: An office gathers the historians' notes
scenes.artBrief: Officials in Joseon robes seated around low tables piled with papers and scrolls, sorting documents in a quiet hall.

scenes.narrationEn: They wrote a first draft, corrected it in a second draft, and polished a final draft. Most of the Annals were then printed with movable type.
scenes.artBrief: Three stacks of paper growing neater from left to right, then a wooden tray of small type blocks and freshly printed pages drying.

scenes.narrationEn: And the used drafts? In early Joseon, they were soaked and washed in a stream near the government paper office. Secrets stayed safe, and the paper could be reused. This was called {kw:secho}.
scenes.captionEn: Used drafts washed in a stream
scenes.artBrief: A clear mountain stream with flat rocks; officials gently rinsing sheets of paper as the ink swirls away, Hoya watching from a rock.

scenes.narrationEn: The finished Annals were kept in special archives called {kw:sago}. During a great war in the 1590s, the copies kept in Seoul, Chungju and Seongju were lost. Only the Jeonju copy survived.
scenes.captionEn: Only the Jeonju copy survives a war

approximations.rationaleEn: The Imjin War began in 1592, which is in the 1590s.

scenes.artBrief: A traditional archive building with a tiled roof and wooden walls; one lantern-lit doorway glowing, suggesting the one surviving copy.

scenes.narrationEn: Two local scholars, An Ui and Son Hong-rok, used their own money to carry the Jeonju copy and other books to Naejangsan Mountain. They took turns guarding them until the books were handed to the government the next year.
scenes.captionEn: Scholars carry the books to a mountain

approximations.rationaleEn: f6 names the two scholars, An Ui and Son Hong-rok.

scenes.artBrief: Two scholars in plain traditional clothes and wide-brimmed hats leading a small ox cart loaded with wrapped book boxes along a misty mountain path.

scenes.narrationEn: After the war, new copies were printed from the Jeonju copy, making five sets. Most went to archives deep in the mountains or on an island, such as Odaesan and Taebaeksan, where war was less likely to reach them.
scenes.captionEn: Copies sent far away, safer from war
scenes.artBrief: A small walled archive compound nestled among pine-covered mountain ridges, clouds drifting below the peaks.

scenes.narrationEn: The books were wrapped in oiled paper and red cloth, then packed in a wooden chest with herbs called cheongung and changpo, which helped protect them from bugs and rot.
scenes.captionEn: Books packed with herbs in a chest
scenes.artBrief: An open wooden chest: books wrapped in red cloth, small cloth pouches of dried herbs tucked at the bottom and on top.

scenes.narrationEn: Every few years, a historian traveled to each mountain archive on a clear day. The books were taken out and aired in the sun and breeze. This was called {kw:poswae}. Hoya loves sunny days, too!
scenes.captionEn: Airing the books in the sun

line.en: We dry the books in the sunshine.
line.speaker: narrator

scenes.artBrief: Books laid open on mats in a sunny courtyard of a mountain archive, a historian checking pages while a breeze lifts them; Hoya basking nearby.

checks.promptEn: In early Joseon, why were used drafts washed in a stream?

options.en: To make the old paper smell fresh again
To turn the ink into a new color
To keep secrets and reuse the paper

checks.explainEn: In early Joseon, used drafts were washed in a stream so secrets stayed safe and the paper could be used again.

checks.promptEn: Who saved the Jeonju copy of the Annals during the war?

options.en: Merchants from a busy market town

checks.explainEn: Local scholars An Ui and Son Hong-rok used their own money to move the Jeonju copy to Naejangsan Mountain and guard it.

options.en: Airing the books in sun and breeze

checks.explainEn: Poswae means taking the books out on a clear day, every few years, and airing them in sunlight and wind.

facts.claimEn: Each king's Annals were compiled after his death, during the next reign, by a temporary office called the Sillokcheong.

facts.claimEn: Compilation went through three drafts (chocho, jungcho, jeongcho); the final draft was the basis for printing, and most of the Annals are printed books made with movable type.
facts.claimKo: 실록은 초초·중초·정초의 3단계를 거쳐 편찬되었고, 정초를 대본으로 인쇄하였으며, 대부분 활자로 인쇄한 간본이다.

facts.claimEn: In early Joseon, used drafts were washed in a stream outside Jahamun Gate, where the government paper office (Jojiseo) was, to prevent leaks and to recycle the paper; this was called secho. In later Joseon, drafts were mostly burned instead.
facts.claimKo: 조선 초기에는 사용한 초고를 조지서가 있던 자하문 밖 차일암 시냇물에 씻어 기밀 누설을 막고 종이를 재생하였는데, 이를 세초라 하였다. 조선 후기에는 대부분 소각하였다.

facts.claimEn: The Annals were kept in archives (sago). In the Imjin War, which began in 1592, the copies at the Chunchugwan in Seoul and at Chungju and Seongju were lost; only the Jeonju copy survived.
facts.claimKo: 실록은 사고에 보관되었다. 1592년 일어난 임진왜란으로 춘추관·충주·성주 사고의 실록은 소실되고 전주사고본만 남았다.

sources.title: 조선왕조실록 정족산사고본 (朝鮮王朝實錄 鼎足山史庫本) – 기본 정보·국가유산 설명

sources.quoteOrLocator: 1592년(선조 25) 임진왜란이 발발하자 ... / 임진왜란을 거치면서 춘추관과 충주· 성주사고의 실록은 소실되었고 전주사고본만 남게 되었다.

sources.title: 실록을 보관하는 곳, 사고
sources.publisher: 국가기록원 (National Archives of Korea), 조선왕조실록의 어제와 오늘
sources.quoteOrLocator: 그러나 임진왜란으로 하나의 실록만 남게 되었으며, 유일하게 남은 전주사고본(『태조실록』~『명종실록』)을 바탕으로 ... (연표: 임진왜란 1592-98, 춘추관사고본, 충주사고본, 성주사고본 소실)

sources.title: 조선왕조실록(朝鮮王朝實錄)

facts.claimEn: An Ui and Son Hong-rok, local Confucian scholars, used their private funds to move the Jeonju copy and other books to Naejangsan Mountain, guarded them in turns, and handed them to the government in 1593, the following year.
facts.claimKo: 선비 안의와 손홍록은 사재를 털어 전주사고본 실록과 서적을 내장산으로 옮기고 번갈아 지키다가 이듬해(1593년) 정부에 넘겨주었다.

sources.title: 조선왕조실록(朝鮮王朝實錄)
sources.publisher: 한국학중앙연구원 한국민족문화대백과사전 (Encyclopedia of Korean Culture)
sources.quoteOrLocator: 전라도 태인의 선비인 안의(安義)와 손홍록(孫弘祿)이 ... 사재(私財)를 털어서 『태조실록』부터 『명종실록』까지 13대의 실록 804권과 기타 소장 도서들을 모두 정읍의 내장산으로 옮겨놓았다. 그리고 이듬해 7월에 정부에 넘겨줄 때까지 1년여 동안 번갈아가며 지켜

sources.title: 조선왕조실록 정족산사고본 (朝鮮王朝實錄 鼎足山史庫本) – 기본 정보·국가유산 설명
sources.publisher: 국가유산청 국가유산포털 (Korea Heritage Service, National Heritage Portal)
sources.quoteOrLocator: 전주 유생 안의(安義), 손홍록(孫弘錄) 등이 전주사고본 실록을 내장산으로 옮김으로써 실록이 병화(兵火)를 면하게 되었다. 전주사고본 실록은 1593년에 조선 정부에 인계되었고

facts.claimEn: After the war (1603–1606), the Annals were reprinted from the Jeonju copy, so that five sets in all were kept in five archives.
facts.claimKo: 전쟁 후(1603~1606년) 전주사고본을 바탕으로 실록을 다시 인쇄하여, 모두 5부를 다섯 곳의 사고에 보관하였다.

sources.title: 조선왕조실록 정족산사고본 (朝鮮王朝實錄 鼎足山史庫本) – 기본 정보·국가유산 설명
sources.publisher: 국가유산청 국가유산포털 (Korea Heritage Service, National Heritage Portal)
sources.quoteOrLocator: 1603년(선조 36) 7월부터 1606년 3월까지 전주사고본을 바탕으로 4부를 재간행하여 춘추관, 강화, 태백산, 묘향산(뒤에 적상산으로 이전), 오대산 등 5곳의 사고에 보관하였다.

sources.title: 조선왕조실록(朝鮮王朝實錄)
sources.publisher: 한국학중앙연구원 한국민족문화대백과사전 (Encyclopedia of Korean Culture)
sources.quoteOrLocator: 1603년 7월부터 1606년 3월까지 2년 9개월 동안에 ... 인쇄, 출판하였다. 이 때 출판한 실록은 3부였으나, 전주사고에 있던 실록 원본과 재출판시의 교정본(校正本)을 합하여 5부의 실록이 갖추어졌다.

facts.claimEn: Apart from the copy kept at the Chunchugwan in Seoul, the sets were placed in archives deep in the mountains or on an island (Manisan on Ganghwa Island, Taebaeksan, Myohyangsan, Odaesan) so they would be safer from war.
facts.claimKo: 서울 춘추관에 둔 1부 외의 실록은 전란을 피할 수 있도록 강화도 마니산, 태백산, 묘향산, 오대산 등 깊은 산속이나 섬의 사고에 보관하였다.

sources.title: 조선왕조실록(朝鮮王朝實錄)
sources.publisher: 한국학중앙연구원 한국민족문화대백과사전 (Encyclopedia of Korean Culture)
sources.quoteOrLocator: 1부는 국가의 참고를 위하여 옛날과 같이 서울의 춘추관에 두었다. 다른 4부는 병화를 면할 수 있는 깊은 산속이나 섬을 선택하여 강화도 마니산, 경상도 봉화의 태백산, 평안도 영변의 묘향산, 강원도 평창의 오대산에 사고

sources.title: 실록을 보관하는 곳, 사고
sources.publisher: 국가기록원 (National Archives of Korea), 조선왕조실록의 어제와 오늘
sources.quoteOrLocator: 전쟁이라는 위기상황에서 접근성이 쉬운 이유로 실록이 불에 타서 사라지는 경험을 하였기 때문에 새로 제작된 실록은 깊은 산 속에 분산 보존하였습니다.

facts.claimEn: The Annals were wrapped in thick oiled paper and then in red cloth, and placed in a wooden chest together with the herbs cheongung and changpo, which were added to prevent insect damage and decay.
facts.claimKo: 실록은 유둔(기름 먹인 두꺼운 종이)으로 싼 다음 다시 붉은 보(홍보)로 싸서, 충해와 부식을 막기 위해 천궁·창포와 함께 궤에 넣어 보관하였다.

sources.title: 실록을 보관하는 곳, 사고
sources.publisher: 국가기록원 (National Archives of Korea), 조선왕조실록의 어제와 오늘
sources.quoteOrLocator: 천궁(川芎)과 창포(菖蒲)라는 약재를 함께 보관하였는데 ... 습기를 막기 위해 기름을 먹인 종이에 실록을 감싸고, 다시 붉은 비단으로 포장합니다.

facts.claimEn: Historians were sent to the archives every few years to take out the Annals and air them in sunlight and wind (poswae), on a clear day; the NIKH and the Encyclopedia of Korean Culture say once every three years, the National Archives every two to three years, and the poswae entry sets the schedule in the jin-sul-chuk-mi (辰戌丑未) years, the same cycle as the civil-service examination years, which recurs every three years.
facts.claimKo: 사관이 몇 년마다 사고에 파견되어 맑은 날을 택해 실록을 꺼내 햇볕과 바람에 말렸다(포쇄). 국사편찬위원회와 한국민족문화대백과사전(실록)은 3년에 한 번, 국가기록원은 2~3년마다, 같은 사전의 포쇄 항목은 과거식년과 같이 진·술·축·미년(3년마다 돌아오는 해)에 시행하도록 했다고 설명한다.

verification.notes: Third independent pass. All Sillok entries (Taejong 4/2/8 #4; Jeongjo 19/leap2/13 #1 and #3) re-fetched from sillok.history.go.kr and compared to original Chinese/Korean text. Every non-UNESCO URL cited was re-fetched fresh and every quote segment machine-matched, plus heritage.go.kr 국가유산 설명 text loaded from the portal's own ajax file (DATA1/heritage/hub_img/html/cul_*.html). UNESCO register pages for all four items verified via Internet Archive (registration years 1997/2001/2007/2011 with exact wording); Uigwe nomination PDF re-extracted and quotes/section numbers verified; Seungjeongwon nomination PDF could not be re-fetched (captcha) so the author's saved text was used, with other sources backing each fact. Corrections this pass: poswae schedule mistranslation (격 2년 = every third year, not every other year), 'dried herbs' removed, ep5 f4 quote exactified, 3 vocab words not appearing in scenes removed, ep5 f8 second source (정병모 판화사적 연구) and ep6 f3 festival official site added, UNESCO locators replaced by exact page wording, ep3 f7 3,045+198 clarification.

authorNotes: Sources disagree on how many sets were newly printed in 1603-1606 (Korea Heritage Service and National Archives: four; Encyclopedia of Korean Culture: three printed plus the original and a proof copy); all agree on five sets in five archives, so narration says 'making five sets'. Poswae frequency also differs slightly (every 3 years in NIKH and the Annals entry; every 2-3 years in National Archives; the 진술축미 schedule of the Encyclopedia's poswae entry, i.e. every third year, though it often slipped), so narration says 'every few years'. Revision: 'red silk' changed to 'red cloth' (the poswae entry says 홍보 'red wrapping cloth'; only the National Archives says silk); the herbs' purpose is now stated generally ('protect from bugs and rot', per the poswae entry and the National Archives) rather than the National Archives' split into cheongung = insects and changpo = germs/fragrance; 'on a sunny day' replaced by 'on a clear day' (supported by two sources); the closing sentence 'Thanks to such care, the Annals survive today' was removed because it was not backed by a fact entry. Secho by washing is limited to early Joseon (later drafts were mostly burned). The Imjin War is mentioned only as 'a great war' with no violent detail. Omitted as out of scope or tragic: later moves to Jeongjoksan/Jeoksangsan, the Qing invasion, colonial-era removal of the Odaesan copy and its loss in the 1923 Kanto earthquake, the Korean War, and the 2006 return.
